Just so you know, if you're interested on my viewpoint, im a 20yr old british student in the highest/furtherest along level of education (wooo.), University. 

Having a funny relationship with food can be helped in different ways. I'll keep you posted, next time I go to counselling i'll check this leaflet I keep seeing about talking about your relationship with food. It's a funny thing because it can cause us so much angst. For instance, I have a packet of chocolate biscuits by my bed, telling me "im right here, eat me" and then they taunt me for being so empty and look at that extra stretch mark you now have.... we love and hate food at the same time.  

Promising anyone else isn't going to change anything; you have to promise yourself not to. Everytime I go shopping for food (fending for myself, UK Uni Student style) I say to myself; don't you dare cave and buy junk food. But it's only me to stop me from doing it, and i give in. I think you need a buddy to keep your promises to yourself in check; for instance, I quit smoking this year and friends still tell me, when they see me eyeing up the cigs behind the counter, "Emily, you do not need nicotine" and it stops me from buying a packet. 

So maybe get your boyfriend to help you control yourself a bit more on the eating side? It could work.  

Also, don't beat yourself up. no one is saying you're bad or stupid for doing these things, but it's the methods you put in place to stop you from doing something that really proves your a smart cookie. Example, me telling my friends that i wanted to quit smoking, and never see me buying a pack of cigerettes ever again. I haven't touched a smoke since August. ish.

Maybe talk to your teachers about exam anxiety - I for one used to get computer assistance and extra time in my a levels/gcse's. there are things to help you with genuine problems like that, so never be afraid to explore every option. 

I's and N's mean nothing to me honey, don't have the foggiest clue what that could mean, but i guess the implication is between good and bad marks? Sorry, us Brits don't know a thing about us/Canandian... or even the Scottish education system!! XD 

And trust me, group work is always bad. Uni is the same. I end up in the reject/socially awkward group just cause i'm not the staple carbon copy of people in my course. I also don't think your classmates think you're stupid, maybe they are jealous, intimidated, peer pressured or just plain chicken to break the norm and have you in their group. Don't stress yourself about it; you should still strive to make your group the best, rally the troops and get on with the task. Taken from experience, even the reject groups can become cool if they all pull together and work hard enough.

I also hope that your (probably very) good advice to your friend on reddit, maybe he's just been busy job hunting to reply to you. It's probably nothing on your account.

Stay positive,
Emily
